claim: arch_schema_loader.md's Interface section: 'Three reads, one per schema... the project and module reads hand back the composed documents' — ProjectSchema()/ModuleSchema() take no arguments, and test_schema_loading.md S1-S3 call them the same way (`schema.ProjectSchema()`, zero args). arch_schema_checker.md's Responsibilities says the future SchemaChecker will 'obtain the composed project and module schemas from the schema module — a spec directory supplies only the optional profile the composition reads.'
authoritative_source: Neither leaf says how a project-specific spec/profile.json reaches the composition behind a zero-argument read. schema.ResolveProfile(specDir) is the only function that reads spec/profile.json, and it requires a directory argument; ProjectSchema()/ModuleSchema() have no parameter to receive one.
evidence: This is a hole, not a contradiction: nothing in test_schema_loading.md exercises a project-specific (non-default) profile through ProjectSchema()/ModuleSchema() — P1-P5 call ResolveProfile and ComposeProjectSchema/ComposeModuleSchema directly. This PR makes the zero-arg reads compose from the built-in default profile (schema.DefaultProfile()), which satisfies every documented scenario (S1-S13, E1-E6, P2's golden equivalence) and matches the literal 'hand back the composed documents' requirement. But a future specDir-aware caller (SchemaChecker, spexmachina-h4gv.19) that needs a *project's* spec/profile.json reflected in validation cannot get that from ProjectSchema()/ModuleSchema() — it would need to call schema.ResolveProfile(specDir) plus schema.ComposeProjectSchema/ComposeModuleSchema itself, bypassing the zero-arg reads entirely, and no leaf currently says that is the intended path.
proposed_fix: Clarify in arch_schema_loader.md and/or arch_schema_checker.md that project-specific composition is reached by calling schema.ResolveProfile(specDir) plus schema.ComposeProjectSchema/ComposeModuleSchema directly, and that the zero-arg ProjectSchema()/ModuleSchema() reads always compose from the built-in default profile (no file consulted) rather than any particular project's spec/profile.json.
